draft.title: The production possibility frontier
card: A production possibility frontier (PPF) is a curve showing the most of two goods an economy can make with all its resources. It assumes the resources and technology stay the same.
the economy is using its resources fully and well. It cannot make more of one good without making less of the other.
some resources are unused or poorly used, such as workers without jobs. The economy could make more of one good, or both, with no loss.
Moving along the curve shows opportunity cost. To make more of one good, the economy gives up some of the other. A point outside the curve cannot be reached with current resources.
draft.remember: On the PPF, more of one good means less of the other. Inside it, resources are wasted.

a.q: An economy is at a point inside its PPF. What does this show?
opts: Some resources are unused or poorly used
Resources are fully used and well used
The economy has more resources than before
The economy is making as much as it possibly can
a.why: Inside the curve, the economy makes less than its resources allow, so some are wasted. Points on the curve, not inside it, show full and efficient use of resources.
a.clue: Compare the point with the most the economy could make.

b.q: Bella's Island can make only coconuts and fish. It moves along its PPF to catch more fish and now makes fewer coconuts. What does this show?
opts: The opportunity cost of more fish is fewer coconuts
Island resources have been wasted by the change
The island has gained more resources and technology
The island can now make more of both goods
b.why: On the PPF, resources are fully used, so more fish means moving workers away from coconuts. The coconuts given up are the opportunity cost. Making more of both would need a point inside the curve moving out to it, not a move along the curve.
b.clue: On the curve, nothing is idle, so where do extra fish come from?

a.best: Some resources are unused or poorly used

b.best: The opportunity cost of more fish is fewer coconuts

problems.detail: Why (b) says making more of both 'would need a point inside the curve moving out to it'. But the island is already on its PPF. From there, making more of both would need the curve itself to shift outward, which needs more resources or better technology. As written, the why could confuse students about the inside-the-curve case.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one clear right answer. The only problem is that Why (b) muddles how an economy already on its PPF could make more of both goods.
